description: A permissions layer that intercepts every agent action — read, write, buy, delete, send, execute — and enforces policy before side effects happen.
notes: Shared kit landed mid-build; app was re-targeted from the fallback Kit to the real shared/kit.js contract (nav actions are now real buttons, modals use fn/primary).

notes.note: Real buyer (security teams), real budget line, and the thesis is directionally right. Weakest assumption: the enforcement point lives with a third-party rather than inside the agent frameworks themselves, which are all building this natively. Crowded lane — every security vendor has a guardrails slide — so this wins on distribution, not technology.
Gatekeep firewall: allow/deny/quarantine triage works; decision feed updates; zero errors.

notes.change: Fixed KPI row landing half-hidden under the fixed nav on load (html scroll-padding-top:132px so scrollIntoView clears the nav).
Added per-agent anomaly detection (README next-3 #3): seeded wire baseline for finance-agent; $8k intercept now also flags 8.9x deviation from its $900 usual; first-seen action types flagged in feed.
